## CAPI-owned production render-event path

Render-origin observation ownership and event staging remain entirely inside CAPI or use an
already accepted non-public capability. Remove the Issue-120 public mutable controller producer and
do not replace it with another public or `doc(hidden)` mutable protocol entrypoint, exported helper,
feature setter, queue injector, event constructor, token factory or generally callable capability.
The protocol may expose only an unavoidable read-only view already authorized by Issue 120; its
wire, queues, replay and staging behavior do not change.

The shipped CAPI path remains bounded, preallocated and completely charged. Render publishes only
fixed observations with atomics or an equivalent accepted bounded realtime-safe handoff. It does
not allocate/free, lock, encode, mutate a controller, destroy, call I/O/syscalls/logging or perform
an unbounded operation. CAPI control/dequeue code owns draining, diagnostic meaning, event staging
and encoding. No retained collection grows after construction, and reliable diagnostic retry plus
lossy meter/counter coalescing/drop behavior stays byte-identical to the Issue-120 literal vectors.

Tests stimulate all six families only through existing exported C commands, source submission,
render and dequeue. No direct protocol queue/stage call, second session/controller, test-only event
producer or mutable setup backdoor may supply an observed event. Preserve invalid-lane, empty,
zero-capacity query, one-short canary/non-consumption, exact retry, reliable FIFO/no-drop and lossy
1/1 counter evidence.
